text:
End-to-end artifact map

Because the platform is unidentified, this shows typical artifacts. Depending on the product, some are generated automatically while others are authored by teams and managed by the platform.

Diagram
flowchart TD
  A[Discovery: goals, stakeholder map, scope, capability map, risk register] --> B[Requirements: stories, use cases, process models, acceptance criteria, traceability]
  B --> C[Architecture: system context, service boundaries, dependency map, architecture decisions]
  C --> D[Detailed design: API contracts, data models, workflow definitions, security model, UI specifications]
  D --> E[Configuration and build: source code, connectors, schemas, migrations, policies, infrastructure definitions]
  E --> F[Testing: test cases, test data, automation suites, scan reports, defects, evidence]
  F --> G[Release: versioned packages, container images, release notes, approvals, software bill of materials]
  G --> H[Deployment: environment configuration, secrets references, deployment manifests, pipeline records]
  H --> I[Operations: logs, metrics, traces, dashboards, alerts, audit records, incident tickets]
  I --> J[Evolution and governance: change requests, lineage, compliance evidence, service catalog, deprecation records]
  J --> B
limitations: The platform’s actual stages and artifact-generation capabilities cannot be confirmed without its identity or documentation.
